name: Memphis Design
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference (not a source collection style name). Uses dots, zigzags, stripes, circles and irregular geometry in bold contrasting colors; patterns set rhythm around a readable headline. Suggestion palette: warm cream #FFF6E8, ink #202039, pink #ED718E, teal #3DBAB1 and yellow #F4C64F. These are optional, noncanonical colors for new work only; task, brand, approved and existing semantic colors take precedence. Keep colors discrete; gradients are disabled. Preserve approved roles, families, asset colors and limits. Contrast ratios are candidates for opaque pairs only; check final compositing.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to playful brand and pattern pieces. Suggested hybrids support vertical social and youth-brand promos with speech-synced emphasis captions, or logo stings, onboarding illustrations and stickers with restrained elastic accents. Interactive HTML may use pinned-hero recomposition, chapter transitions or scroll storytelling when they clarify the content. Those motion patterns are optional and their scene suitability must be checked; omit pinning if it disrupts layout, crops detail or forces unsafe text placement.
limitations: Keep headlines readable; limit simultaneous movement and avoid rapid full-frame flashing. Do not let captions cover faces or subtitles; deform only a few hero shapes, preserve apparent area, and never deform headlines. Omit chaptering when it obscures causal links, breaks continuity or adds needless complexity. Pinning must not jump on release or depend on live scroll in video. Claims are design guidance, not evidence of source production methods.
palette: Bold contrast is explicit; the five hex values and pink/teal/yellow direction are suggestions only. Resolve colors from task exact values, approved brand/reference palette, existing semantic mapping, then suggestions. Normalize equivalents only; do not recolor artwork, alter approved hues or roles, or add colors. Use one dominant background and clear foreground hierarchy; accents stay subordinate except in bold geometric fields. No gradient. Suggested opaque text pairs: ink on cream (14.769), pink (5.541), teal (6.674) or yellow (9.824); cream on ink (14.769). Meet 4.5 normal-text target where applicable, but recheck actual size, texture, transparency, imagery and compositing; use an existing backing or reposition text if needed.
motionAndInteraction: Build reusable SVG patterns and shape groups; stagger selected movement, elastic offsets and pattern handoffs rather than moving everything. GSAP is the primary suggested motion engine; Motion or mo.js are optional and must synchronize with shared seekable time. Mo.js can add geometric bursts, shapes or swirls, but not arbitrary path morphs, physics, character rigs or music analysis. Give each property one owner; seed randomness and make state deterministic for direct, reverse and out-of-order seeks. For interactive HTML, optional patterns map finite scroll progress to staged states, with accessible reading order, reduced-motion behavior, keyboard/touch checks and stable pin entry/release. Video must use composition time, never live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the subject and objective; honor supplied requirements and assets. Suggest mood, energy, tempo, voice delivery and scene changes where useful. Do not assume assets exist. Synchronize and mix through the render pipeline; check intelligibility, competing vocals, clipping and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Use SVG for scalable geometry, patterns, icons, strokes, masks and clipping. Optional @remotion/shapes supplies standard SVG forms; Canvas 2D is an alternative. Load local fonts and assets, preserve exact copy and approved artwork/colors, and separate layers when they need independent motion. Export any tldraw-authored diagrams as deliberate layers; a flattened image is not editable. Cache stateful simulations and seed randomness. Inspect representative frames and full playback for legibility, crop, outlines, missing assets, timing and audio sync.
combinations: Works alone for playful brand and pattern pieces. With style-115 emphasis captions, map emotion to the three accent colors, keep outlines #202039 and animate one pattern at a time; captions need live-region text and responsive face clearance. With style-106 squash and stretch, deform only selected shapes, preserve apparent area and keep patterns still. Optional motion-007 pinned hero, motion-012 chapter handoff and motion-015 storytelling are conditional candidates, not required effects; use only when supported by the actual scene and narrative.
productionApproach: Choose visual renderer and motion method for style, action, assets and fidelity before the pipeline; state each responsibility. SVG owns drawing, GSAP the primary motion timeline, and optional libraries only their justified effect. HyperFrames is the default composition/export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, documenting why. Neither pipeline replaces visual or motion design. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers; inspect decoded opening, action, transition and closing frames and full video, then verify dimensions, duration, frame rate, loop, audio and synchronization. For HTML, test applicable scroll, keyboard, touch and reduced-motion behavior.
